xu322s8.author: Plato
xu322s8.label: Philosophers practise dying
xu322s8.translation: For I deem that the true votary of philosophy is likely to be misunderstood by other men; they do not perceive that he is always pursuing death and dying; ... Is it not the separation of soul and body? And to be dead is the completion of this; when the soul exists in herself, and is released from the body and the body is released from the soul, what is this but death?
xu322s8.reading: Death here is the release of the soul from the body: dis-identification from the bodily dimension and consciousness turning toward itself. Socrates uses two verbs, dying and being dead, because it is a daily process of removing one identification at a time. She links λανθάνειν, "escape notice", to λήθη.

xkljean.work: The Golden Verses and Iamblichus' Life of Pythagoras
xkljean.author: Pythagorean tradition; Iamblichus
xkljean.label: If you leave the body for the free aether
xkljean.translation: Letting intelligence o’er thy body reign; / So that, ascending into radiant Ether, / Midst the Immortals, thou shalt be thyself a God.
xkljean.translator: Nayán Louise Redfield (1917), English version of Fabre d'Olivet's French rendering
xkljean.reading: She stresses that the Greek says ἤν, "if", not "when": leaving the body at death is not liberation, because you can die full of wants and soon return. Freedom is whenever we drop the illusion that we are the body. (Redfield's English, made from a French verse version, does not keep the "if".)
